QUOTE: NONE
VERDICT: MISS
WHY: The answer says the library and two test programs define the opt-out and see plain names while default consumers see renamed ones, but it never ties this to one macro choosing between two branches that give different consumers different views of the same header — it frames it as audiences, not the two-view spelling mechanism.

Correction: that WHY undersells what the answer says. The answer does state that without the define `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member)` becomes `private_##member`. It also states that where the define is present (`library/common.h`, `ssl_server2.c`) it becomes plain `x`, and the table lists the two sets of consumers. That is the item's substance, so the verdict should be a HIT.

QUOTE: "The library itself | `library/common.h:132` defines it unconditionally | `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(x)` becomes plain `x` in every library `.c` that includes `common.h`." and "Unless `MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS` is defined, `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member)` expands to `private_##member`"
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says code defining the macro sees plain member names and ordinary consumers of the public headers see the renamed `private_` ones.
